questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was interested in the culture of Central and North America

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: At the orientation, you are sufficiently filled in on courses and registration - There are plenty of other exchange students, so it is easy to set up groups to figure out stuff

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would suggest living off campus; my impression was that the dormitories on campus have strict security, which i would not have enjoyed

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was fine - i lived in a house i found through an organization called Cholula Capital. Naturally it is not luxury housing; Often times problems with water heating, and dirty common areas, but i think that is just a part of it; at least i was prepared for that. 
My landlord was a tricky one though; he has not payed my deposit back, I dont expect to get it...

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Easy to figure out; They publish the relevant course lists quite late in the process though. Other than that there are people to help you with everything.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There are a few "incoming coordinators" that help you with everything from course registration to printing copies of your passport for the internationals office - in that sense it was quite easy. The orientation tells you everything you need to know.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty succesful; I enrolled in four out five first priorities.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take it easy - you can handle most problems that may occur, when you get to UDLAP.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 3 of my courses were way to easy to be Uni level. 2 of them were more challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching resembles Gymnasium in DK - There is a lot of homework compared to back home, a lot of assignments and a limited amount of absence. Most of the work is relatively easy compared to my education back home though.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: History of International Relations, Humanist thought, Sociolinguistics, Psychotherapy and Communication and Globalization.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Humanist Thought was a great philosophical course ! I would recommend taking any courses that is taught by Francisco Iracheta; All in all a great instructor, a very inspiring guy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: ADO busses for travelling - i travelled almost every week, which was one of my main priorities, and the busses are nice and safe, but a bit expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things are quite cheap; ADO busses to get around in the country can be a bit expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not do a lot of extracurricular things at UDLAP, but i know that they have opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dancing, music, singing and sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I knew a few people who took salsa lessons, which they were very impressed by

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as you can ! Oaxaca, Chiapas, CDMX !

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the local dancing clubs to learn salsa, do the sunday flee markets, do sports at campus

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The holidays ... Day of the dead, independence day, new years

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Stay somewhere off campus

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: In my opinion, don't listen to people who tell you Mexico is not safe; As long as you use common sense, everything will be fine - The mexicans are a great, welcoming and chill people

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends i made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I dont feel like i had any

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
